title: Sindhu Marches to Round of 16 as Shetty Stuns World Number One at BWF World Championships
excerpt: PV Sindhu advances to face Wang Zhi Yi in a blockbuster Round of 16, while Ayush Shetty delivers the upset of the tournament by knocking out defending champion Shi Yuqi on home soil in New Delhi.
body:
• PV Sindhu, seeded ninth, has advanced to the Round of 16 at the 2026 BWF World Championships in New Delhi, where she will face third seed Wang Zhi Yi of China in a blockbuster matchup.
  • Ayush Shetty delivered the tournament's biggest upset on Day 1, stunning defending champion and world number one Shi Yuqi of China 21-14, 13-21, 21-19 in front of a raucous home crowd.
  • India is hosting the World Championships for the first time in 17 years, with the event at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium running through August 23.
  • Sindhu boasts a perfect 7-0 record against Chinese opponents at the World Championships, spanning over a decade of competition.

The 2026 BWF World Championships have delivered drama from the opening day, with India's shuttlers seizing the spotlight at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi. PV Sindhu, the five-time World Championship medallist and 2019 gold winner, has advanced to the Round of 16 where a critical clash against third seed Wang Zhi Yi of China awaits. Meanwhile, 21-year-old Ayush Shetty has announced himself on the world stage with a stunning first-round upset of defending champion Shi Yuqi.

Sindhu Eyes Unprecedented Sixth Medal

Sindhu entered the tournament as the ninth seed, arriving in New Delhi on the back of her Japan Open triumph last month. The draw placed her in the top half, with a manageable early path before the difficulty escalates sharply. Her Round of 16 opponent, Wang Zhi Yi, is ranked third in the world and represents one of China's brightest young talents.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=uk7b6dicqbM

But the history books favor Sindhu. Her record against Chinese opponents at the World Championships stands at a remarkable 7-0, stretching back to her debut in 2013. She has beaten Wang Yihan, Wang Shixian, Li Xuerui, Sun Yu, and Chen Yufei across multiple editions — never once falling to a Chinese shuttler on this stage.

Against Wang Zhi Yi specifically, the head-to-head is tighter at 3-5, with their last three encounters going to a deciding third game. But Sindhu's ability to elevate her performance at the World Championships — where she has medaled in five of nine appearances — makes her the more dangerous player in a tournament setting.

"Crowd was really behind and gave me the energy. They kept cheering for me. It gave me a lot of energy."

— Ayush Shetty, after defeating world number one Shi Yuqi

Shetty's Breakthrough Moment

If Sindhu's campaign has been methodical, Ayush Shetty's has been seismic. The 21-year-old from Karkala, Karnataka, made his World Championships debut by taking down the tournament's top seed and defending champion Shi Yuqi 21-14, 13-21, 21-19 — his first victory over the Chinese star in four meetings.

Shetty, who won a silver medal at the Badminton Asia Championships earlier this year, built an 11-5 lead in the decisive third game before holding off a late Shi fightback. The victory reversed their most recent meeting, when Shi had dispatched Shetty in just 40 minutes during the Asia Championships final in April.

The result has galvanized the home crowd and injected energy into an Indian campaign that also features 14th seed Lakshya Sen in men's singles, fifth seeds Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty in men's doubles, and 15th seeds Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto in mixed doubles.

India's Medal Streak on the Line

India have produced at least one World Championships medal at every edition since 2011, an 11-tournament streak built by Sindhu, Saina Nehwal, Kidambi Srikanth, Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy, and the Satwik-Chirag pairing. With the tournament returning to Indian soil for the first time since Hyderabad in 2009, the pressure to extend that run is immense.

National coach Pullela Gopichand has expressed confidence in the squad's depth. "Overall it looks like a good draw from an Indian perspective," he said ahead of the tournament. On Shetty's draw against Shi Yuqi, Gopichand noted: "Given Ayush's attacking game, it is better to play Shi first up than later in the tournament."

What to Watch

Sindhu's Round of 16 match against Wang Zhi Yi is the marquee encounter for Indian fans. A win would set up a potential quarterfinal against sixth seed Putri Kusuma Wardani of Indonesia, who eliminated Sindhu at the 2025 World Championships in Paris. Beyond that, a semifinal collision with world number one An Se Young — who holds a 10-0 record against Sindhu — looms as the ultimate test.

For the Indian diaspora following from abroad, the home World Championships carries an emotional charge beyond the medals. It is a chance to see an entire generation of Indian badminton talent competing on the biggest stage, in their own country, with a crowd that has already shown it can be a decisive factor.
